name: Williamsburg
_poi_role_reasoning: A neighborhood with split character experienced by walking its streets, trigger_radius 400m.
_poi_role_source: walk the streets peopled by this sect

beats.script_body: Until the late 19th century, Williamsburg was mainly where Manhattan's elite came for a weekend away from the city. It didn't officially become part of New York City until 1898, when Brooklyn became a borough. Then the Williamsburg Bridge was completed in 1903, putting a crossing of the East River within reach of the average person. Newly arrived immigrants and people fleeing the packed tenements of the Lower East Side flooded into Brooklyn, and Williamsburg became one of the most densely populated neighborhoods in the city.
beats.source_passage: Until the late 19th century, Williamsburg, in Brooklyn, was primarily a place where the Manhattan elite came for a weekend away from the big city. It didn't officially become part of New York City until 1898, when Brooklyn became a borough of New York City. The completion of the Williamsburg Bridge in 1903 made it possible for the average person to travel across the East River. Newly arrived immigrants and those escaping the packed tenement buildings of the Lower East Side soon flooded into Brooklyn, and Williamsburg became one of the most densely populated neighborhoods in the city.

beats.script_body: Brooklyn has always been a melting pot, and that's still visible in Williamsburg. The neighborhood originated in what is now South Williamsburg, where there are significant populations of Hasidic Jews, Puerto Ricans, and Dominicans. The northern part, known as the North Side, is home to large Polish and Italian communities. In recent years many young Manhattanites have made the move across the water, and Williamsburg has become one of Brooklyn's hippest, most popular neighborhoods — artists and creative types were the trailblazers, but a growing influx of young professionals now lives in luxury waterfront apartments with a view of the city.
beats.source_passage: Brooklyn has always been a melting pot of cultures, and this is still very visible in Williamsburg today. Williamsburg originated in what is now South Williamsburg. Here there are significant populations of Hasidic Jews, Puerto Ricans, and Dominicans. The north of Williamsburg, known as the North Side, is home to large Polish and Italian communities. Recent years have seen many young Manhattanites making the move across the water, and Williamsburg has become one of Brooklyn's hippest, most popular neighborhoods.

beats.script_body: In creative Williamsburg, street art is a way of life. Nowhere else in New York City will you find so many murals, stickers, and stencils on walls, facades, lampposts, doors, mailboxes, curbs, or just about anywhere. Pay attention and you'll start to notice the recurring work of certain artists throughout the neighborhood.

name: Williamsburg Bridge
short_description: A 1903 steel-frame suspension bridge linking Williamsburg and the Lower East Side; at the time the longest suspension bridge on earth, with foot and bike paths offering East River views.
_poi_role_reasoning: A bridge with foot/bike paths you cross for East River views, traversed rather than stood at a single point.
_poi_role_source: The bridge's all-steel towers and foot/bike paths with East River views

beats.script_body: The Williamsburg Bridge connects Manhattan and Williamsburg, carrying cars and trucks but also a separated path for cyclists and pedestrians. The view of eastern Manhattan from the Williamsburg side is amazing, and because foot and bike traffic is kept apart from vehicles, crossing is both safe and pleasant.

physical_cues.cue: View of eastern Manhattan from the Williamsburg side of the bridge

beats.source_passage: The Williamsburg Bridge connects Manhattan and Williamsburg. It is used by cars and trucks, but you can also cross by bicycle or on foot. The view of eastern Manhattan from the Williamsburg side is amazing, and since cyclists and pedestrians are separated from the rest of traffic, getting to the other side is both safe and pleasant.

name: Williamsburg Art & Historical Center
short_description: Williamsburg's best-known art gallery, housed in the former Kings County Savings Bank building at 135 Broadway; shows American and international painting, sculpture, installation, and modern art.

beats.script_body: The Williamsburg Art & Historical Center is housed in the original Kings County Savings Bank — an ornate 1860s building that still stands as a New York City landmark. Today it is the best-known gallery in the neighborhood, with exhibits that change regularly and range from paintings and sculptures to installations and modern art by both American and international artists.

name: City Reliquary
short_description: Tiny niche neighborhood museum. Quick gravity: low.
_poi_role_reasoning: A tiny discrete niche museum with interior display cues, a single stop.
_poi_role_source: A tiny museum that seems to take its aesthetic from flea markets

beats.script_body: The tiny City Reliquary Museum is definitely not your average museum — it's packed with rare artifacts tied to the history of New York City. There's a replica of the Bay Ridge Barbershop, which operated in Brooklyn for 50 years, along with a collection of items from the 1964 World's Fair held in New York. The gift shop carries fun, interesting pieces by local artists.

name: Republic of Booza
short_description: Williamsburg ice cream shop billed as the first in the United States to sell booza, an elastic, creamier Levantine ice cream whose recipe dates back roughly 500 years.

beats.script_body: Republic of Booza was the first shop in the United States to sell booza, an ice cream invented about 500 years ago in the eastern Mediterranean. Ice cream as we know it descends from booza, but booza is more elastic and creamier, with a richer taste. The ancient recipe arrives here in a hypermodern, almost Japanese interior, alongside experimental flavors like Chinese pepper with Oreo cookies.

Booza ice cream was invented about 500 years ago in the eastern Mediterranean. Ice cream as we know it, is based on booza, but booza is more elastic and creamier and has a richer taste.

name: The Knitting Factory
short_description: A well-known name on the New York music scene; like The Bitter End and Arlene's Grocery, it has given a stage to then-unknown punk, pop, rock, and funk acts. Williamsburg location at 361 Metropolitan Ave.

beats.script_body: The Knitting Factory is a well-known name on the New York music scene. Like The Bitter End and Arlene's Grocery, it has given a stage to then-unknown punk, pop, rock, and funk acts that went on to become legends. Maybe the next Nirvana will be on stage during your visit.

name: Partners Coffee
short_description: Williamsburg coffeehouse on North 6th Street that began as Toby's Estate, specializing in Australian-style coffee; still serves 'short blacks' and 'flat whites' alongside small-batch roasted beans.

beats.script_body: Partners Coffee began life as Toby's Estate, which specialized in Australian coffees. The company had its roots in Australia, where owner Toby Smith started roasting his own coffee, and years later it opened its first American location here in Williamsburg. Partners still pours "short blacks" and "flat whites" alongside small-batch roasted beans.

name: Filthy Rich Barbershop
short_description: Williamsburg barbershop on Havemeyer Street, an institution since 2006 known for trendy cuts and for styling well-known rappers.

beats.script_body: Williamsburg is a hipster mecca, often pictured as the land of beards and man buns, so a great barber is essential. Filthy Rich Barbershop has been an institution here since 2006, giving trendy cuts and even styling famous rappers.
beats.source_passage: At Filthy Rich Barbershop they not only give you a trendy haircut, they also style famous rappers like Big Sean and Flo Rida. It's been an institution since 2006.

name: The Gutter
short_description: One of Williamsburg's three bowling alleys, on North 14th Street; opened in 2007 with a 1950s-throwback interior and old-fashioned board games for waiting bowlers.

beats.script_body: In Williamsburg people appreciate a beer and a good game of bowling — the neighborhood has three bowling alleys, and The Gutter is one of them. Although it only opened in 2007, once you step inside you'll feel you're back in the 1950s. If you have to wait for a lane, you can pass the time over an old-fashioned board game.

name: Brooklyn Brewery
short_description: A Williamsburg craft brewery offering tours and tastings, whose cursive logo was designed by Milton Glaser of 'I Heart New York' fame.
_poi_role_reasoning: A discrete brewery venue you visit, small radius.
_poi_role_source: the Brooklyn Brewery brews local suds and offers 45-minute tours of its facilities

beats.script_body: During the week, Brooklyn Brewery is open only for tours. But starting Friday afternoon at 5pm a line begins to form at the door as people wait for the tasting room to open. The beers are inexpensive by NYC standards, and though there isn't much in the way of food, the brewery doesn't mind if patrons have a pizza delivered.

name: East River State Park
short_description: A 7-acre Williamsburg waterfront park with Manhattan views and cobbled vestiges of its cargo past; summer home to Smorgasburg, the country's largest outdoor food market.
_poi_role_reasoning: A 7-acre waterfront park you walk through, named as a park.
_poi_role_source: This 7-acre waterfront park is a slice of greenery with sublime views of Manhattan

beats.script_body: With its spectacular view across the river to Manhattan, East River State Park is a fine place to relax and take a few photos. On Saturdays, when the Smorgasburg market sets up here, the park doubles as a great spot for fresh, tasty snacks and treats.
